source.title: Cross-Layer Interaction under Weight-Space Ablation: A Closed-Form Attention Jacobian Bound and a Test on a Real Pretrained Model

page_placements.theme: Non-additive effects of joint ablation (within heads, across layers, between head groups)

record.tranche_reason: The paper cites the Hydra effect and notes a shared-plus-idiosyncratic circuit pattern, but does not test whether ablation causes downstream self-repair. Its own ablation experiments measure cross-layer interaction and circuit collapse, not restoration by later components.
record.gate_note: The paper's own weight-edit and zero-ablation results are recorded as related findings under fits_no_version: they do not measure compensation or restoration as specified by any claim version. The Hydra-effect result is cited from prior work and is not recorded as a row. The paper also measures patching-versus-ablation dissociation, which is not a self-repair measure.
record.test_reason: The paper cites the Hydra effect only to frame the shared-plus-idiosyncratic IOI circuit pattern. Its own experiments measure weight-edit interaction decompositions, circuit collapse ratios and patching-versus-ablation gaps. None measures later components restoring output after an ablation, so it does not test any self-repair version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The paper adds three results: an exact multi-layer decomposition (same-block terms plus a cross-layer remainder), an exact two-layer identity for that remainder, and a closed-form attention Jacobian bound verified with zero violations on Qwen weights, though not chained across layers. On Qwen IOI, a shared head (L25H9) appears across all five instances. Collapse and dissociation occur on most instances but not all. A nonzero interaction appears on three instances at non-same-block pairs, so it bears on the open multi-layer case rather than the companion theorem.
record.recipe_differences: The paper does not reproduce a Hydra-style layer ablation and downstream-restoration measurement. It uses weight edits of selected carrier subspaces on synthetic-task checkpoints and joint zero-ablation of pruned IOI circuits on Qwen; its IOI circuit search uses activation patching.
record.method_sensitivity: The marker-task interaction results vary with ablation configuration; the Qwen collapse ratio varies by IOI instance, and the interaction probe applies only to three instances with both a head and an MLP in the circuit.

fits_no_version.finding: Pooled over 1440 multi-layer marker-task pair-configurations, the median cross-layer remainder (0.59) is roughly twice the same-block sum (0.31) and the total interaction (0.30). The terms often partially cancel.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under multi-layer weight-space ablation, non-additive cross-layer interaction is routinely as large as or larger than same-block interaction.

fits_no_version.finding: Two heads at different layers with no MLP give a large same-block sum that largely cancels the cross-layer remainder (3.85 vs total 0.11). A head+MLP configuration gives terms closer to the total (0.21 vs 0.37).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The balance between same-block and cross-layer interaction depends on which components are jointly ablated.

fits_no_version.finding: Jointly zero-ablating a 6-site IOI circuit in Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct narrows the branch gap to between 0.168 and 0.396 on four instances. On Anna/Mike it barely narrows the gap (0.761).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Joint ablation of a patching-discovered circuit can leave much of the conditional behaviour intact on some instances, consistent with redundancy outside the found circuit.

fits_no_version.finding: For three non-same-block head/MLP pairs in Qwen, the joint-ablation effect differs from the sum of the single ablations by a relative 0.066 to 0.327. No sign rule predicts the direction.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In pretrained transformers, the effects of ablating two components at different layers are non-additive.

record.code_released: not stated (scripts and repository paths are named, but no URL is given)
record.problems: The paper does not directly measure self-repair or restoration by later components. The pretrained-model evidence is from one model and five IOI instances; the interaction probe applies to only three. The authors also state that their chained multi-layer Jacobian bound is unverified and likely loose.
record.rows_left_out: The paper's patching-versus-ablation dissociation gaps were left out because they compare different intervention estimands rather than measuring compensation. Circuit-search recovery values were also left out because they measure activation-patching search recovery, not ablation-induced repair.

untested.parts: No single attention-layer ablation with measurement of downstream attention compensation.
No late-MLP logit analysis of maximum-likelihood token erasure or how it changes under earlier ablations.
No single-head ablation measuring compensation on general text across model families or sizes.
No per-prompt distribution of compensation and no overcorrection measure.
No identification of backup heads, copy-suppression heads, LayerNorm rescaling or anti-erasure neurons.
Only zero ablation and data-estimated projector edits; no comparison of self-repair under mean or resample ablation.
No test of whether self-repair distorts ablation-based importance scores. The patching-versus-ablation dissociation concerns different estimands, not compensation.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's classification is confirmed. All rows correctly carry versions ["none"] with state cannot_determine. Table 1's interaction column is an absolute relative magnitude, so it cannot show compensation direction. The only signed value given in the text, Sarah/Tom −R× = −0.117, does not measure restoration either. Cited self-repair work (Hydra effect; Gong et al. on dormant backups) is not re-tested here. The single-author preprint is dated 2026 and its code repository has no URL.

versions.untested_parts: No test of ablating one attention layer and measuring later attention layers restoring the original output.
No test of late-MLP downregulation of the maximum-likelihood token or its change after earlier ablations.
No single-head ablation test of partial compensation on the full output distribution across models or sizes.
No measurement of prompt-level variation or overcorrection in self-repair.
No test identifying backup heads, copy-suppression heads, final LayerNorm rescaling, or anti-erasure neurons as self-repair mechanisms.
No comparison of mean or resample ablations with zero ablation for self-repair.
No test of whether self-repair makes ablation-based importance scores misstate component function.

relation.reason: Self-repair findings provide related-work context for shared and instance-specific circuit components; they are neither tested nor used as an experimental tool.

tranche.reason: The experiments measure interaction decompositions, circuit collapse and patching–ablation dissociation, without measuring downstream compensation or testing another self-repair claim version.

source_check.notes: Interaction magnitudes do not establish self-repair. The sign discussion identifies no general rule; the authors explicitly caution that three Qwen observations cannot settle a statistical sign relationship.
